original_question: Find a general property of a lifting family in the interval version of Thurston’s algorithm that guarantees convergence for arbitrary kneading sequences, not only preperiodic or periodic ones.
target_in_paper: §3, Question 4: "Give a general property for the lifting family which will guarantee convergence of Thurston's algorithm for arbitrary kneading sequences."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact subsection (§3, the interval/real version of Thurston's algorithm), the right object to constrain (the lifting family used in place of polynomial lifts), and the right scope distinction: the target is the arbitrary-kneading-sequence version, not the neighboring preperiodic/periodic version. In substance, it is very close to Question 4 and also correctly echoes its contrast with Question 3.
missing_details: The ambient space is not stated: P = P(n,μ), the space of piecewise monotone maps f:I=[0,1]→I with n laps and prescribed boundary map μ:{0,1}→{0,1}.

The draft does not define the interval Thurston iteration itself: starting from f0∈P, one chooses a lift p0 in P with the same critical values, in the same order, as f0, then a unique homeomorphism h0:[0,1]→[0,1] with p0∘h0=f0, and continues inductively.
It does not say explicitly that the lifting family is a family inside P used in place of the polynomial lifts p_k in that inductive construction.
It omits the ordered-critical-values condition, which is part of how the lift is selected.
It omits the conjugacy update f_{k+1}=h_k∘f_k∘h_k^{-1}, which is part of the algorithmic setup immediately preceding Question 4.
It does not quantify over the initial map f0 (or, equivalently in context, over all kneading sequences realized by maps in P(n,μ)).
It does not specify the normalization I=[0,1] and the boundary condition on {0,1}.

It leaves 'convergence' unattached to the actual iterative scheme; a stand-alone version should tie convergence to the Thurston iteration built from the chosen lifts, while remaining faithful to the paper's intentionally informal wording.
refined_question: In the setting of §3, fix P=P(n,μ), the space of piecewise monotone maps f:I=[0,1]→I with n laps and prescribed boundary map μ:{0,1}→{0,1}. Starting from any f0∈P, run the interval Thurston algorithm but, instead of taking polynomial lifts, choose at each step a lift p_k from a fixed family F⊂P having the same critical values as f_k, encountered in the same order, and let h_k:[0,1]→[0,1] be the unique homeomorphism sending the critical points of f_k to those of p_k with p_k∘h_k=f_k, so that f_{k+1}=h_k∘f_k∘h_k^{-1}. What general property of the lifting family F is sufficient to guarantee convergence of this Thurston iteration for arbitrary kneading sequences, without restricting to the preperiodic or periodic case?
justification: This paper is a problem list, and the nearest official formulation matching your draft is not a theorem or conjecture but §3, Question 4 on page 9. The surrounding setup on pages 8-9 defines the real/interval version of Thurston's algorithm, including the ambient space P=P(n,μ), the polynomial lift p0 with the same ordered critical values as f0, the homeomorphisms h_k, and the inductive construction of f_{k+1}. The immediately preceding Question 3 is the preperiodic/periodic-kneading analogue, so your draft's contrast phrase is faithful; the refined version simply restores the paper's full setup and keeps the scope exactly at Question 4.
